N-1.1-A.skill: use average rates over shrinking intervals computed from position values to estimate an instantaneous rate and separate it from averages and amounts

N-1.1-B.skill: reason about how a strictly monotone instantaneous rate relates to the average rate over an interval and to midpoint values

N-1.2-A.skill: evaluate a limit of f(g(x)) by determining from which side the inner expression approaches the point, using one-sided limit notation

N-1.2-B.skill: set one-sided limits equal to find a parameter for which a two-sided limit exists, ignoring the function value at the point

N-1.3-A.skill: read a verbally described graph at several points and distinguish where a finite limit exists from where the function value, one-sided behavior or unbounded growth interferes

N-1.3-B.skill: combine one-sided limits read from two graphs to evaluate a sum, difference or product whose two-sided limit exists even though the factors' limits do not

N-1.4-A.skill: estimate two limits from tables of values near a point where both functions are undefined, then combine them

N-1.4-B.skill: judge what a table of sampled values can and cannot establish about a limit

N-1.5-A.skill: recover individual limits from limits of linear combinations using limit properties, then evaluate a new expression

N-1.5-B.skill: decide what the limit laws force about one function when a combination and the other function have limits

N-1.6-A.skill: choose the constant that makes a 0/0 form removable, factor, and evaluate the resulting limit

N-1.6-B.skill: evaluate a 0/0 limit by combining a complex fraction or rationalizing a radical

N-1.7-A.skill: select the procedure of combining fractions over a common denominator for a difference of unbounded terms

N-1.7-B.skill: split a limit into a special trigonometric limit and a rational factor and combine the pieces

N-1.8-A.skill: apply the Squeeze Theorem to a bounded oscillating factor inside a product and then add a constant

N-1.8-B.skill: identify where two quadratic bounds meet so the Squeeze Theorem applies, and recognize it applies nowhere else
